entry.title: Practical Feng Shui: Arranging Your Space to Actually Change Your Life
entry.summary: Forget the mysticism — practical feng shui is about designing spaces that reduce friction, increase clarity, and quietly support the life you're building.
entry.content:
I used to roll my eyes at feng shui. Crystals, mirrors facing the door, lucky bamboo — it all felt like aesthetic advice pretending to be something deeper. Then I started noticing how my actual environment affected my focus, mood, and energy day to day. The conclusions I reached mapped almost perfectly onto what feng shui practitioners have been saying for centuries. Just without the incense.

This isn't about belief. It's about environmental design. Your space is always working on you — the question is whether it's working for you or against you.

The Command Position

The single most impactful feng shui concept is the "command position." The rule: place your bed, desk, and stove so you can see the door while using them — without being directly in line with it.

Here's why it works: when you can see the entrance, your nervous system settles. You're not unconsciously startled by someone walking in. When your back faces a door, part of your brain stays on guard. Over hours and years, that low-grade vigilance drains energy you could spend on better things.

Try this: - Angle your desk so you see your room or office entrance. Can't? A small mirror reflecting the doorway does the trick. - In the bedroom, position the bed diagonally from the door — you should see it from where you lie, but not be directly in line with it. - Wherever you prepare food, make sure you're not facing a wall with your back exposed.

Repositioning your most-used furniture often produces more visible improvement than any other single change.

Clear the Pathways

Feng shui talks about energy flow. In plain terms: obstructed pathways create obstructed thinking.

Hallways stuffed with clutter, doors that don't open fully, having to squeeze between objects — your brain registers constant micro-friction. You might not consciously notice it, but it's there. A background process eating attention.

Try this: - Every door should open fully without hitting anything. - Walk your home's natural paths (entrance → living area → bedroom → bathroom). Remove what forces you to step over, squeeze past, or navigate around obstacles. - If a room feels "heavy," check what's blocking movement. Usually it's one large item in the wrong spot.

The Five Elements as Design Constraints

Feng shui's five elements — wood, fire, earth, metal, water — aren't mystical forces. They're a framework for visual variety.

A room that's all metal and glass feels cold. All wood and fabric feels heavy. No contrast feels flat. The elements are a reminder to mix textures and materials:

Element Represents Design Expression
Wood Growth, vitality Plants, vertical lines, natural wood
Fire Energy, passion Lighting, candles, warm colors
Earth Stability, grounding Ceramics, earth tones, low furniture
Metal Precision, clarity Metallic finishes, round shapes, white/gray
Water Flow, calm Mirrors, glass, dark colors, asymmetry

Try this: Walk through your main living space. If one element dominates, add a touch of another. A sterile metal desk gets a small plant. A heavy wooden room gets a mirror or white ceramic. The goal isn't perfect balance — it's variety.

Kill the Dead Space

Every home has corners where things go to die. Closets that haven't been opened in years. Surfaces covered in "I'll deal with this later."

Stagnant clutter blocks flow. In practical terms: visual clutter competes for your attention. Every object in your field of vision is something your brain has to process, categorize, and decide to ignore. That's cognitive load you don't need.

Try this: - Haven't used it in 12 months and it's not seasonal? Candidate for removal. - Flat surfaces (tables, counters, desks) should be 60–70% clear. The empty space isn't wasted — it's breathing room. - The area directly inside your front door matters more than you'd think. It's the first thing you see when you come home. Keep it clean, well-lit, intentional.

Light and Air Are Not Optional

The most underrated part of environmental design: lighting and air quality directly affect cognitive performance and mood.

Feng shui calls it "bright energy." Science calls it circadian regulation and CO₂ levels. Same thing, different vocabulary.

Try this: - Maximize natural light. Ditch heavy curtains if you can. Clean your windows — dirty ones filter out more light than you'd expect. - Warm light (2700–3000K) in bedrooms and living areas. Save cool/blue light for task lighting. - Open your windows at least 10 minutes daily. Stale air makes stale thinking. - Room feels oppressive? Check the lighting first. Often the room isn't the problem — the bulbs are.

The Entryway Is Everything

Your front door is where energy enters. Practically: it's the transition point between the outside world and your inner sanctuary.

Walk into darkness, clutter, or a wall of stuff, and your brain never gets the signal that you've "arrived home." You carry the outside world's energy with you.

Try this: - Entrance should be well-lit. No natural light? Add a warm lamp. - Get shoes, coats, and bags out of the immediate entry area. Give them designated storage just inside. - Add one thing that signals "this is my space" — a plant, art, a scent. Something sensory that marks the transition.

What This Isn't

Let me be straight about what practical feng shui is not:

  • Not about buying specific objects for specific areas of your home.
  • Not about compass directions or auspicious dates.
  • Not about believing in energy you can't measure.
  • Not a substitute for fixing real problems — leaks, pests, broken furniture, poor ventilation.

It is about treating your environment as a tool — one that either supports or undermines your focus, rest, and clarity every single day.

Start With One Room

Don't try to feng-shui your entire home in a weekend. You'll burn out and revert.

Start with the room where you spend the most waking hours. Apply these:

  1. Put your primary furniture in command position.
  2. Clear all pathways.
  3. Remove everything from flat surfaces that doesn't serve a purpose.
  4. Add or improve lighting.
  5. Introduce one element that's missing.

Live with it for a week. Notice what changes. Then move to the next room.

Your space is the stage on which your life happens. Most people never think about the stage — they just keep performing on it and wondering why everything feels harder than it should.

Rearrange the stage. The performance follows.

This week's been a blend of learning, exploring, and vibing to some timeless tunes. From diving into plain text accounting to picking up JavaScript basics and getting lost in thrilling movies, here's what shaped my week.

Articles

  • Plain Text Accounting Basics — A clear intro to PTA, breaking down how tools like Beancount can simplify financial tracking. Perfect for getting a grip on money without bloated apps. Inspired me to refine my ledger setup and track expenses more intentionally.

Exploring

  • OceanofPDF — Stumbled across this site for free PDF books. Spent hours browsing titles on finance, coding, and self-improvement. A goldmine for knowledge seekers, though I'm double-checking the legality of downloads to stay on the right side.

Tutorial

  • JavaScript for Beginners — Watched this YouTube tutorial to kickstart my JavaScript journey. Covers variables, functions, and DOM manipulation with clear examples. Practiced building a simple counter app, which felt like a small win. Next step: tackling arrays and loops.

Music

Vibed to a mix of classics that hit the soul:

  • Fallin' — Alicia Keys. That piano riff and raw emotion — pure magic.
  • Stuck on You — Lionel Richie. Smooth, nostalgic, and perfect for late-night reflection.
  • Jolene — Dolly Parton. A storytelling masterpiece with heart-wrenching vocals.
  • Take Me Home, Country Roads — John Denver. Felt like a mental road trip to hunt for peace.
  • DNA (Tom's Diner) — Suzanne Vega. A quirky, hypnotic vibe that stuck in my head all week.

Movies

  • Predator: Killer of Killers (2025) — Three legendary warriors face off against an ultimate predator in a brutal, action-packed hunt. The tension and stakes kept me glued to the screen.
  • The Amateur (2025) — A CIA decoder goes rogue after his wife's death in a terrorist attack. Intense and emotional, with twists that hit hard.
  • Sinners (2025) — Twin brothers return home to escape their past, only to face a darker evil. A chilling story with a haunting atmosphere.

Another week of growth, inspiration, and stories that spark the mind. Ready for what's next!

entry.title: Setting Up Cronie and Scheduling Scripts in Termux
entry.summary: A step-by-step guide to installing cronie in Termux and scheduling scripts to run at specific times on Android.
entry.content:
Setting Up Cronie and Scheduling Scripts in Termux

Cronie is a powerful tool for scheduling recurring tasks in Termux, allowing you to automate scripts on your Android device without root access. This guide walks you through installing cronie, setting up cron jobs, and managing them effectively, with examples tailored for Termux users.

Why Use Cronie in Termux?

Cronie enables you to run scripts at specific times or intervals, perfect for tasks like backups, notifications, or syncing files. Unlike termux-job-scheduler, which is better for periodic tasks with Android-specific conditions (e.g., battery level), cronie offers precise, time-based scheduling similar to Linux cron. However, Android’s power management may kill Termux, so a wake lock is recommended.

Prerequisites

  • Termux installed from F-Droid (not Google Play Store).
  • Scripts you want to schedule (e.g., Bash, Python) in a known path (e.g., $HOME/scripts/).
  • Basic familiarity with Termux commands and a text editor like nano or vi.

Step 1: Install Cronie and Termux-Services

  1. Update Termux packages: pkg update && pkg upgrade
  2. Install cronie and termux-services: pkg install cronie termux-services

Step 2: Enable Cronie Service

Enable the crond daemon to run cron jobs:

sv-enable crond

If you see an error like “unable to change to service directory,” restart Termux and retry. Verify crond is running:

sv status crond

Step 3: Create and Schedule Cron Jobs

  1. Open the crontab editor: crontab -e This opens the default editor (usually vi). If you prefer nano, set it first: export EDITOR=nano crontab -e
  2. Add cron job entries using the cron syntax: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week command. For example: ``` # Run a script every day at 8:00 AM 0 8 * * * /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/backup.sh

# Run a Python script every Monday at 9:00 AM 0 9 * * 1 /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/python /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/notify.py

# Run a script every hour 0 * * * * /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/sync.sh 3. Save and exit (`:wq` in `vi`, or `Ctrl+O`, `Enter`, `Ctrl+X` in `nano`). 4. Verify cron jobs: crontab -l ```

Example Scripts

Backup Script (backup.sh)

Create a script to back up files:

#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash
mkdir -p $HOME/backups
tar -czf $HOME/backups/backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz $HOME/storage/documents

Make it executable:

chmod +x $HOME/scripts/backup.sh

Schedule it to run daily at 8:00 AM:

0 8 * * * /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/backup.sh

Notification Script (notify.py)

Create a Python script to send a Termux notification:

#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/python
import os
os.system('termux-notification -t "Weekly Reminder" -c "Time to review your goals!"')

Make it executable:

chmod +x $HOME/scripts/notify.py

Schedule it to run every Monday at 9:00 AM:

0 9 * * 1 /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/python /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/notify.py

Step 4: Prevent Termux Termination

Android may kill Termux in the background, stopping cron jobs. To mitigate: - Acquire a Wake Lock: termux-wake-lock Run this before starting crond to keep Termux active. Note: This may drain battery, so use sparingly. - Disable Battery Optimization: Go to Android Settings > Apps > Termux > Battery > Disable optimization. - Optional: Termux:Boot: Install Termux:Boot from F-Droid, enable it, and add termux-wake-lock to $HOME/.termux/boot/ scripts to run on device startup.

Troubleshooting

  • Cron Jobs Not Running:
  • Check if crond is active: sv status crond.
  • Ensure script paths are absolute (e.g., /data/data/com.termux/files/home/scripts/backup.sh).
  • Verify script permissions: ls -l $HOME/scripts/backup.sh (should show -rwxr-xr-x).
  • Logs: Check cron logs at $PREFIX/var/log/sv/crond/current for errors.
  • Termux Killed: Re-run termux-wake-lock and sv-enable crond after app restarts.

Cronie vs. Termux-Job-Scheduler

  • Cronie: Best for precise, recurring schedules (e.g., daily at 8:00 AM). Requires Termux to stay active.
  • Termux-Job-Scheduler: Better for periodic tasks with Android conditions (e.g., run when charging). Less precise but more battery-friendly. Example: termux-job-scheduler -s $HOME/scripts/backup.sh --period-ms 3600000

Tips

  • Use crontab.guru to craft cron schedules.
  • Test scripts manually before scheduling: bash $HOME/scripts/backup.sh.
  • Keep Termux open or use a wake lock for reliable cron execution.
  • For one-time tasks, consider at (if available) or termux-job-scheduler with a script to check the date.

Automate your tasks with cronie and take control of your Termux workflow!

entry.title: Normalize Silence: Finding Greatness in Stillness
entry.summary: Embracing silence to build resilience, clarity, and greatness in a distracted world.
entry.content:
Normalize Silence: Finding Greatness in Stillness

In a world screaming for your attention—social media notifications pinging, Afrobeat blasting, and the hustle of Lagos life pulling you in every direction—silence is your superpower. As a Nigerian chasing big dreams, you need to normalize silence to unlock the clarity and strength that set you apart.

Why Silence Matters

Greatness isn’t born in the noise of the crowd or the endless scroll of Instagram. It’s forged in the quiet moments where you face yourself. Silence strips away distractions, forcing you to confront your thoughts, fears, and ambitions. It’s where you hear the voice of your purpose, loud and clear, like a Harmattan breeze cutting through the chaos.

Most people run from silence. They drown it with music, conversations, or Netflix marathons because being alone with their thoughts feels like standing naked in Computer Village—exposed and uncomfortable. But you? You’re not most people. You’re a hustler with a vision, and silence is your training ground.

How to Embrace Silence

Here’s how to make silence your ally, Naija style:

  • Train Without Music: Hit the gym or do your push-ups in your room with no earbuds. Let the rhythm of your breath and the burn of your muscles be your soundtrack. Feel every rep, every sweat drop. This builds mental toughness, like a danfo driver navigating Lagos traffic without losing focus.

  • Eat Without Distractions: No phone, no TV, no gist. Sit with your plate of jollof or egusi and savor each bite. Notice the flavors, the textures. This isn’t just eating—it’s a meditation that grounds you in the present, teaching you to find joy in simplicity.

  • Sit Alone with Your Thoughts: Find a quiet corner—maybe your balcony or a park bench in Surulere. No gadgets, no company, just you and your mind for 10 minutes. Let your thoughts roam like okadas on a free road. Don’t judge them; observe them. This is where you uncover what’s holding you back and what’s pushing you forward.

The Power of Stillness

When you learn to be bored without grabbing your phone, to be still without needing company, and to be alone without feeling lost, you’re building discipline. You’re training your mind to stay sharp in a world that thrives on distraction. This is the secret of the greats—think of Dangote closing billion-naira deals or Burna Boy crafting Grammy-winning lyrics. Their power comes from moments of solitude, where they connect with their inner fire.

In Nigeria, where every day is a hustle, silence is a rebellion. It’s saying, “I don’t need the noise to know who I am.” It’s where you dream bigger than the skyline of Victoria Island, plan smarter than a Lagos trader, and grow stronger than the iroko tree.

Your Challenge

Start today. Spend 10 minutes in silence—no music, no phone, no distractions. Do it while eating, walking, or just sitting. Feel the discomfort, then push through it. Journal what comes up—your fears, your dreams, your next move. Do this daily, and in 30 days, you’ll notice: - Sharper focus, like a hawk spotting opportunity in a crowded market. - Deeper self-awareness, knowing your strengths and weaknesses like a well-read book. - Unshakable calm, ready to face any storm, from NEPA blackouts to life’s bigger battles.

Keep It Real

Greatness isn’t found in the likes, the followers, or the noise. It’s built in the stillness where most refuse to go. As a Naija hustler, you know the grind never stops—but it’s in the quiet moments that you sharpen your edge. Normalize silence, and watch your life transform into something louder than words. 🗣️🔉🔊

Let’s rise above the noise, one silent moment at a time.
